high_level_overview.overview: This program is part of the CardDemo application, a credit card management system that maintains cross-reference data linking card numbers to their associated account identifiers. It operates as a batch reporting utility within the account management workflow, typically run to audit or verify the integrity of card-to-account mappings. The program sequentially reads and displays all records from the account cross-reference VSAM indexed file (KSDS), providing a printed listing of every card number and its corresponding account data. It solves the operational need to inspect and report on the complete cross-reference dataset without modifying any records.

key_features.description: Reads all records from the account cross-reference VSAM KSDS file in sequential order from beginning to end
Displays each cross-reference record showing the 16-digit card number and its associated 34-byte account data
Detects and gracefully handles end-of-file conditions, terminating the read loop cleanly when all records have been processed
Identifies and reports file I/O errors during open, read, and close operations with detailed file status codes
Calls the CEE3ABD system routine to force a controlled program abend with code 999 when unrecoverable errors are encountered
Translates and displays numeric or non-numeric file status codes to assist in diagnosing file access issues
Uses dedicated paragraphs to open and close the cross-reference file with proper status checking at each step

input_output.name: XREFFILE
input_output.description: Account cross-reference VSAM KSDS file - read sequentially to retrieve card cross-reference records containing card number (16 chars), customer ID (9 digits), and account ID (11 digits). Each record is displayed to standard output as it is read.

data_flow.description: Program begins execution, displays start message, and initiates the file open sequence
Opens XREFFILE as an indexed VSAM KSDS file in sequential input mode. Validates file status code '00' for success. On failure, displays error, logs IO status, and abends the program
Iterates through all records in the cross-reference file sequentially until end-of-file is reached. The END-OF-FILE flag controls loop termination
Reads the next sequential record from XREFFILE into CARD-XREF-RECORD (defined in CVACT03Y copybook). Evaluates file status: '00' for success, '10' for end-of-file, any other value triggers an abend

Displays the contents of CARD-XREF-RECORD to standard output (SYSOUT). Record is displayed both within the read routine (on successful read) and in the main loop body, resulting in duplicate display per record
When file status '10' is returned, APPL-RESULT is set to 16 (APPL-EOF condition), and END-OF-FILE flag is set to 'Y', terminating the read loop
Closes XREFFILE after all records have been processed. Validates file status '00' for success. On failure, displays error, logs IO status, and abends the program
Displays end-of-execution message and returns control to the calling environment via GOBACK

On any unrecoverable I/O error, IO-STATUS is populated, 9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS formats and displays the two-byte file status code (handling both numeric and non-numeric status values including VSAM extended codes), then 9999-ABEND-PROGRAM calls CEE3ABD with abend code 999 to terminate abnormally

data_dependencies.description: The XREFFILE VSAM KSDS must be successfully opened in paragraph 0000-XREFFILE-OPEN before any read operations in 1000-XREFFILE-GET-NEXT are attempted. A failed open triggers an immediate abend, preventing any reads

The CARD-XREF-RECORD structure is entirely defined by the CVACT03Y copybook. The program depends on this copybook to correctly map the 50-byte record (16-byte card number + 34-byte data) read from XREFFILE into named fields for display and processing

The main processing loop depends on the END-OF-FILE flag being initialized to 'N'. The flag is only set to 'Y' within 1000-XREFFILE-GET-NEXT upon receiving file status '10'. Any corruption of this flag would cause an infinite loop or premature termination

APPL-RESULT drives all post-I/O branching logic. It uses 88-level condition names APPL-AOK (value 0) and APPL-EOF (value 16). The open routine pre-sets it to 8 before the OPEN statement to ensure a non-zero value if the OPEN verb itself fails silently

All I/O outcome decisions depend on the two-character XREFFILE-STATUS field populated by the COBOL runtime after each file operation. The program explicitly checks for '00' (success) and '10' (EOF); all other values are treated as fatal errors

XREFFILE is defined with ACCESS MODE IS SEQUENTIAL. This means records must be processed in key order (FD-XREF-CARD-NUM ascending) and no random or dynamic access is possible. The program has no capability to seek to a specific card number

CARD-XREF-RECORD is displayed twice per record: once inside 1000-XREFFILE-GET-NEXT on a successful read, and once in the main loop body after the paragraph returns. This is a logical dependency issue where the main loop's display is redundant and dependent on the read paragraph not having already displayed the record

The abend paragraph 9999-ABEND-PROGRAM depends on the LE (Language Environment) runtime routine CEE3ABD being available in the execution environment. This routine is called with TIMING=0 and ABCODE=999 to force an abnormal termination with a user abend code

external_system_integrations.purpose: CEE3ABD is called to force an abnormal program termination with user abend code 999 when an unrecoverable I/O error occurs. This is an IBM z/OS Language Environment callable service used for controlled abend processing

error_handling.description: In 0000-XREFFILE-OPEN, after attempting to open the XREFFILE, the FILE STATUS is checked. A status of '00' sets APPL-RESULT to 0 (AOK); any other status sets it to 12. If not AOK, an error message is displayed, IO-STATUS is populated, 9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS is performed to format and display the status code, and 9999-ABEND-PROGRAM is called to terminate the program abnormally.

In 1000-XREFFILE-GET-NEXT, after each READ, FILE STATUS is evaluated: '00' sets APPL-RESULT to 0 (AOK), '10' sets it to 16 (EOF), and any other status sets it to 12 (error). EOF condition gracefully sets END-OF-FILE to 'Y' to exit the read loop. Any other non-AOK status triggers an error message display, IO-STATUS formatting via 9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS, and program abend via 9999-ABEND-PROGRAM.

In 9000-XREFFILE-CLOSE, after the CLOSE operation, FILE STATUS is checked. A status of '00' zeroes APPL-RESULT (AOK); any other status sets it to 12. If not AOK, an error message is displayed, IO-STATUS is populated, 9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS is performed, and 9999-ABEND-PROGRAM is called to force an abnormal termination.

The 9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS routine handles both numeric and non-numeric (e.g., VSAM system-specific) file status codes. For non-numeric or '9x' statuses, it converts the binary second byte into a numeric representation using TWO-BYTES-BINARY redefinition. For standard numeric statuses, it formats the two-character status into a four-digit display field. The formatted status is then displayed to the operator for diagnostics.

The 9999-ABEND-PROGRAM routine provides a centralized abnormal termination mechanism. It displays 'ABENDING PROGRAM', sets TIMING to 0 and ABCODE to 999, then calls the IBM Language Environment routine 'CEE3ABD' to force a controlled program abend. This ensures that unrecoverable errors result in a clean, identifiable failure rather than silent continuation.
